request: Cores um pouco mais vivas, sem exagero e sem tom sombrio.

prompts.base:
Use case: precise-object-edit, color grading only. Edit the supplied game character image. User wants clothing colors A LITTLE MORE VIVID and explicitly says it DOES NOT need a gloomy/dark tone. Use a brighter, clear, welcoming classic fantasy RPG palette, moderate color saturation, not gloomy desaturated brown/grey. Garment midtones about15-20% more saturated and12-15% lighter than input, keeping natural shadow depth, fabric folds and clean pixel details. Greens should read as natural fresh forest green/olive, navy as clear medium royal/navy blue rather than near-black, purple as readable plum/violet with warm gold rather than near-black, brown leather as warm chestnut, red mantle as warm red. Silver steel remains naturally neutral with slightly clearer highlights. Beige linen stays warm ivory, not yellow/orange. No neon colors, no fluorescent runes, no excessive contrast/glow. This is a small tasteful color lift, NOT a redesign, NOT a dark-fantasy grade.
CRITICAL INVARIANTS: exact original character identity, face, skin tone, brown hair, anatomy, clothing design, pose, pixel clusters, contours, hands/feet positions, scale, silhouette and layout. Keep SKIN, HAIR and facial details unchanged. Recolor existing garments/leather details only, no repainting shapes, no new objects, no blur/airbrush, no added weapons, no outline changes. Keep genuine transparent alpha background and all spaces between limbs transparent, no floor or shadows, no colored backdrop. Preserve the original pixel-art character and image aspect. This image contains ONE complete man only. Keep him in exactly the same place with the same surrounding transparent canvas. Give his olive trousers a modestly fresher natural olive green and the linen shirt a clearer warm ivory; boots and belt a subtle warmer chestnut. Face, hair, shirt pattern, lace-up collar and all edges stay exactly the same. No armor.
